contracts.commit_point: middleware.py line 80: result = handler(request) — the point where the agent tool call is actually executed; the blocked path returns the error ToolMessage at lines 74-78 before this statement, so a blocked call never commits.
contracts.declared_mechanism: secure_middleware(mode='enforce') builds Config/Interceptor and returns wrap_tool_call(_make_tool_call_handler(interceptor, session, ToolMessage)), registering the guard into LangChain v1's agent middleware tool-call dispatch (middleware.py:96-109). The _securevector callback serializes the tool-call args and calls Interceptor.evaluate_input, which in order: resolves permissions via resolve_permission (AppUnreachable -> Decision(True,'block','local app unreachable (fail-closed)') in enforce, allow in observe) at core.py:103-109; honors verdict.action=='block' as Decision(self.enforce,'block',...) at core.py:111-118; and runs secret/threat analysis via analyze, blocking only when enforce and risk_score >= cfg.threat_risk_threshold at core.py:127-137. Decision.blocked already accounts for mode and is only True when the call should actually be stopped (core.py:54-63, 17-20). When decision.blocked, _securevector returns tool_message_factory(content='[SecureVector] Tool ... blocked: ...', tool_call_id=call_id, status='error') WITHOUT calling handler (middleware.py:71-78); only otherwise does it reach handler(request) (middleware.py:80).
contracts.forbidden_condition: Control reaching the tool-execution statement handler(request) with Decision.blocked == True under enforce mode, where blocked is caused by any of: (a) LocalAppClient.resolve_permission returning verdict.action == 'block'; (b) a threat/secret finding on the serialized tool input with risk_score >= cfg.threat_risk_threshold; or (c) AppUnreachable during permission resolution (enforce is fail-closed, so an unreachable app yields blocked=True).
pending_binding_information: No runtime source in the supplied views constructs an agent with this middleware; the wiring middleware=[secure_middleware(mode='enforce')] in create_agent appears only in the module docstring example (middleware.py:10-16), so the concrete live agent registration is unconfirmed.
Runtime mode, enabled flag, and threat_risk_threshold derive from Config.from_env environment parsing (middleware.py:106); the deployed enforce configuration cannot be fixed from source.
The semantics of LocalAppClient.resolve_permission verdicts and analyze risk scoring are outside the supplied views (core.py:104, 123).
The session id is a random uuid generated once at middleware construction (middleware.py:108); its binding to a specific agent conversation is not established.
contracts.protected_operation: Execution of an agent tool call through the wrap_tool_call handler path — the _securevector(request, handler) callback invoking handler(request) for the tool identified by request.tool_call['name'] with request.tool_call['args'].
contracts.protected_resource: Agent tools dispatched through the LangChain/LangGraph wrap_tool_call middleware on agents constructed with secure_middleware (tool calls carrying name, args, and id from the agent's ToolCallRequest).
contracts.protection_obligation: In enforce mode, a LangChain/LangGraph agent tool call must not execute when SecureVector's evaluation marks it blocked — i.e., when the local-app policy denies the tool id, when the tool input's secret/threat risk score is at or above the configured threat_risk_threshold, or when the local app is unreachable (fail-closed). The registered wrap_tool_call middleware must short-circuit such a call by returning an error ToolMessage instead of invoking the tool handler. (Merged from first- and second-phase reviewer opinions, which state the same obligation with overlapping citations.)
scope_limits: Blocking occurs only when cfg.mode == 'enforce'; the default 'observe' mode is fail-open and never blocks (core.py:17-20, 106-109, 118, 128; middleware.py:92-93).
No protection when cfg.enabled is false: evaluate_input returns Decision(False,'allow','sdk disabled','') immediately without any checks (core.py:97-98).
Secret/threat analysis is best-effort: AppUnreachable during analyze after permissions pass sets a_in=None and cannot block (core.py:121-125).
Output-side scanning (scan_output) runs only after the tool has already executed and is log-only; it cannot retract a committed execution (core.py:148-157; middleware.py:81-83).
The mechanism requires the LangChain v1 middleware API (langchain.agents.middleware.wrap_tool_call) and raises ImportError otherwise (middleware.py:96-104).

Only tool calls routed through this middleware on agents constructed with it are gated; direct tool invocation outside the middleware and the CrewAI raising convenience path (guard_input, core.py:176-179) are outside this contract.

missing_information: No supplied source view shows a concrete, non-docstring agent/tool registration invoking secure_middleware; the agent wiring exists only as the create_agent example in the middleware module docstring (middleware.py:10-16).

The LocalAppClient implementation (resolve_permission, analyze, record_audit) is outside the supplied views, so permission-verdict semantics and risk-score/threshold comparison behavior cannot be confirmed from source.

Behavior labels / runtime test evidence are unavailable per the stated scope, so actual enforcement behavior in a running agent is unverified.
